issue.title: TestContainers fail to run on Docker 24.x (3.29.3)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/51009 hardcodes docker api version to 1.44 (change done with https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/51002).


`ResettableSystemProperties` were used to instantiate TestContainers and 
[DefaultDockerClientConfig](https://github.com/docker-java/docker-java/blob/main/docker-java-core/src/main/java/com/github/dockerjava/core/DefaultDockerClientConfig.java#L236) takes system properties with highest priority.

This is unfortunately a breaking and non-fixable change for Docker < 25 due to api incompatibility as there is no way for me to influence the `api.version` property passed to `docker-java`.

I can not currently use newer Docker engine version as I am running builds on BuildJet.

Would it be possible to at least respect `api.version` system property if it is set? Or provide an alternative property / env var.

I have also mentioned this issue in testcontainers repo (https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/issues/11232), as they have also made a breaking change with 2.0.2 (but in that case I was able to overwrite `api.version` property). Seems the best course of action would be if they implemented version negotiation.

body: I checked git blame and found the root cause. While the logic to set a default API version has existed for 5 years, the default value was recently updated to VERSION_1_44 (about 3 weeks ago). [The java file is here](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/blame/main/core/src/main/java/org/testcontainers/dockerclient/DockerClientProviderStrategy.java) The Problem: Docker Engine v24 supports up to API v1.43. By forcing v1.44, Testcontainers breaks compatibility for all v24 users. Proposed Fix: We should either: Revert the default value to a safe baseline (e.g., 1.35 or 1.41). Or simply remove this default setting block to let docker-java negotiate the version automatically (which seems to be the preferred behavior for compatibility). If there are no objections, I can submit a PR to remove this block (or downgrade the version).

The problem is that while Docker Engine v24 supports up to API v1.43, Docker Engine v25 supports starting from API v1.44. So, there is no version that is compatible with both.

So, no default setting will satisfy everyone. Either people with the older version or with the newer version of Docker will need to use a "workaround". Therefore, "revert the default" will not do any good because there is no safe baseline.

> let docker-java negotiate

Are you sure `docker-java` will do this? Will negotiate? If yes, then this could be a good solution. If no, then `testcontainers-java` should do the negotiation, in my opinion.

issue.title: Fix Docker API version incompatibility by removing forced default version

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body:
# Motivation
Fixes #11232

In #11216, a default fallback to VERSION_1_44 was introduced in DockerClientProviderStrategy. However, this change broke compatibility for users running older Docker versions (e.g., Docker v24 supports up to API 1.43) because the client forces a newer API version than the server supports.

Since docker-java supports auto-negotiation when the version is null (UNKNOWN), strictly pinning it to 1.44 is unnecessary and causes regressions for legacy environments.

# Changes
Removed the block that forces VERSION_1_44 when the API version is unknown.

This restores the behavior of relying on docker-java's auto-negotiation (or safe defaults).

# Verification
I have verified this fix locally on the following environments:

Docker v29.1.2 (API 1.52, Min 1.44): Passed. (Auto-negotiated correctly)

Docker v24.0 (dind, API 1.43): Passed. (Auto-negotiated correctly)
